name: sdlc-skills
description: Two plugins for coding agents: agentic-dev writes stories by interviewing you and builds them, or a smaller task, against checks the agent writing the code never sees, with hooks that decide when it is done and house rules for how the agent works with you; xp-templates writes and reviews spikes.

plugins.name: agentic-dev
plugins.description: Two skills that take any change from a request to a merge, against checks the agent writing the code never sees: a task skill for a change one check proves done, which asks at most one clarifying question and for the check, hides the check, and has a subagent make it pass from the simplest solution up in its own worktree; and a story skill for a feature or a whole product, which interviews you until nothing is ambiguous, confirms the acceptance criteria in plain language, splits them into vertical-slice stories with a walking skeleton first and files them, then builds one story at a time: a reviewed plan, design choices settled with you, hidden failing tests, slices of at most 200 lines each built as a task and reviewed, a final review and verification, a merge request watched to merge, and the UAT. Plus a prototyping skill for throwaway experiments, reviewer and verifier agents, and hooks for a done check that runs every test and the linter, an AGENTS.md size cap, a dependency gate, gates on commits that leave in debugging leftovers, switch a checker off, or change, remove or skip a test the branch started with, a gate that hides a check from the agent writing the code, a slice cap, a gate on the first edit no skill framed, and a gate on a pull request or merge no reviewer preceded.

plugins.name: xp-templates
plugins.description: A spike skill: the 4 frame lines (decision, falsifiable question, finish line, timebox), the checks a spike is reviewed against, and the finding record. Stories, PRDs and the interview moved into agentic-dev's story skill.
